name: Question 12
problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{{e}^{t}+1}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨1,\sqrt{2},1⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨1,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by T(t)=1et+1⋅q(t). Find the principal normal vector at the point where t=0, if q(0)=⟨1,2,1⟩,q′(0)=⟨1,22,0⟩.

a
 111⟨22,−1,−2⟩
b
 12⟨1,0,−1⟩
c
 12⟨−1,2,−1⟩
d
 13⟨1,0,2⟩
e
 13⟨−2,1,0⟩
